properties.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
properties.description: Landing area of NASA's Perseverance rover in Jezero Crater.
properties.scienceReason: Provides the mission's reference location for exploring the crater floor, delta deposits and ancient lake environments.
properties.why: Useful as the starting point for the Jezero exploration map and route-planning demonstrations.
properties.survivalNote: Use local elevation and slope data; do not assume the landing area is uniformly smooth.

properties.name: Perseverance Delta Exploration Waypoint
properties.description: Project waypoint representing Perseverance's exploration area near the western delta of Jezero Crater.
properties.scienceReason: The delta preserves sediment deposited where an ancient river entered a crater lake.
properties.why: Highlights the geological record of water transport and sediment deposition.
properties.survivalNote: Delta terrain can include scarps, layered outcrops and loose sediment; inspect slope and imagery before routing.
properties.source: NASA Mars 2020 Jezero mission context; project waypoint coordinate.

properties.name: Belva Crater
properties.description: Impact crater feature identified in the team's Jezero-area map review.
properties.scienceReason: Crater interiors and ejecta can expose or redistribute geological materials, useful context for terrain interpretation.
properties.why: Adds a recognizable landform for map orientation and terrain-risk discussion.
properties.survivalNote: Crater rims and interiors may be steep; coordinate is a team map reading and needs orbital-image verification.
properties.source: Team map coordinate; verify feature identity and position against orbital imagery.

properties.name: Hartwell Crater
properties.description: Impact crater feature identified during the team's Jezero-area map review.
properties.scienceReason: Impact structures provide local relief and can expose subsurface materials.
properties.why: Useful as a terrain landmark and candidate area for comparing crater-related hazards.
properties.survivalNote: Treat rim slopes and ejecta blocks as potential obstacles; coordinate is a map reading.
properties.source: Team map coordinate; verify against USGS Gazetteer and orbital imagery before operational use.

properties.name: Neretva Vallis
properties.description: Named inlet valley in the Jezero region.
properties.scienceReason: Fluvial landforms and the associated delta record past water flow and sediment transport into Jezero.
properties.why: Important for reconstructing the ancient drainage and lake system.
properties.survivalNote: Valley walls and channel margins may be uneven or steep; regional science marker, not a safe path.

properties.name: Una Vallis
properties.description: Officially named valley in the broader Jezero study area.
properties.scienceReason: Provides a mapped example of Martian valley morphology and regional drainage.
properties.why: Useful as a geographic and geomorphic reference point.
properties.survivalNote: Do not route along the valley based on this centre point; inspect local slopes and terrain.

properties.name: Sava Vallis
properties.description: Officially named valley in the broader Jezero region. The supplied map point [77.48, 18.85] is retained as a separate map reference, not the official centre.
properties.scienceReason: Provides regional context for Martian valley networks and the hydrologic history around Jezero.
properties.why: Useful for regional science context, but its official centre is outside the current elevation grid.
properties.survivalNote: Valley margins may be steep or rough; this is a regional centre point, not a traversable waypoint.

properties.name: Roubion Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance's Roubion crater-floor sampling locality in the Máaz formation; the attempted core disaggregated during sampling.
properties.scienceReason: The site documents basaltic igneous rocks on the Jezero crater floor and the diversity of the Máaz formation.
properties.why: A published rover sampling location with a peer-reviewed coordinate.
properties.survivalNote: Rock fragments and uneven outcrop surfaces may impede travel; inspect high-resolution imagery and slope data.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474.

properties.name: Rochette Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance collected the Montdenier and Montagnac basalt cores at the Rochette outcrop.
properties.scienceReason: The basalt samples help characterize the igneous history and alteration of Jezero's crater-floor rocks.
properties.why: A published sample site showing where rover science directly investigated crater-floor bedrock.
properties.survivalNote: Outcrop relief and scattered rocks can create local obstacles; use terrain layers before routing.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474.

properties.name: Brac Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance collected the Salette and Coulettes cores from the Brac outcrop in the Séítah formation.
properties.scienceReason: The samples are ultramafic cumulate rocks, providing evidence about the igneous composition and evolution of the crater floor.
properties.why: A peer-reviewed sampling locality representing the Séítah geological unit.
properties.survivalNote: Layered and fractured outcrops may be rough; avoid steep or block-rich surfaces.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474.

properties.name: Issole Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance collected the Robine and Malay cores at the Issole outcrop near the mapped Séítah–Máaz boundary.
properties.scienceReason: The ultramafic samples help constrain the composition of the Séítah unit and its relationship to adjacent crater-floor materials.
properties.why: Useful for illustrating geological contacts and rover sampling strategy.
properties.survivalNote: Contact zones may have variable rock texture and relief; inspect local slope and imagery.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474.

properties.name: Sid Sample Site
properties.description: Perseverance collected the Hahonih and Atsah cores at the Sid outcrop in the Ch'ał member of the Máaz formation.
properties.scienceReason: The samples are andesitic igneous rocks and contribute to understanding the diversity of Jezero's crater-floor lithologies.
properties.why: A published rover sampling locality with direct scientific value.
properties.survivalNote: Rocky outcrops and loose surface material may complicate traversal; confirm the local hazard grid.
properties.source: Simon et al. (2023), JGR: Planets, https://doi.org/10.1029/2022JE007474.

properties.name: Three Forks Sample Depot
properties.description: Approximate map placement for Perseverance's backup depot, where ten sample tubes were deposited in a mapped zigzag pattern near the base of the ancient delta.
properties.scienceReason: The depot preserves a documented backup collection of samples from Jezero's geological environments.
properties.why: A major mission landmark and scientifically important sample cache.
properties.survivalNote: NASA describes the depot ground as relatively flat, but local rocks, dust and approach conditions still require terrain checks. Do not use this approximate centre for precision navigation.
properties.source: NASA/JPL-Caltech sample depot map: https://science.nasa.gov/resource/perseverances-three-forks-sample-depot-map/; coordinate is approximate, not an individual tube coordinate.

properties.name: Amalik Outcrop
properties.description: Approximate map placement for the Amalik outcrop, a Perseverance sampling locality on the Jezero fan front.
properties.scienceReason: Perseverance collected the sedimentary samples Shuyak and Mageik here. Fine-grained, clay-bearing sedimentary rocks are relevant to evaluating ancient aqueous environments and possible biosignature preservation.
properties.why: A scientifically significant sedimentary sampling locality; exact coordinate needs rover traverse or image-based verification.
properties.survivalNote: Outcrop surfaces may be layered, fractured or locally steep; do not treat this approximate point as a safe waypoint.
properties.source: NASA Amalik sampling report: https://science.nasa.gov/blog/perseverance-activities-at-amalik-outcrop/; AGU study https://doi.org/10.1029/2024AV001241; coordinate approximate.

properties.name: Wildcat Ridge
properties.description: Approximate map placement for the Wildcat Ridge outcrop in the Hogwallow Flats member of the Shenandoah formation.
properties.scienceReason: Perseverance collected the sedimentary samples Hazeltop and Bearwallow here; these rocks are important for studying delta-front deposits and potential biosignature preservation.
properties.why: A scientifically significant sedimentary sampling locality; exact coordinate needs rover traverse or image-based verification.
properties.survivalNote: Layered sedimentary outcrops can have uneven surfaces and local scarps; verify exact rover coordinates before routing.
properties.source: AGU study: https://doi.org/10.1029/2024AV001241; Shenandoah Formation study https://doi.org/10.1029/2023JE008187; coordinate approximate.

properties.name: Marysville Crater
properties.description: IAU-adopted impact crater in the broader Jezero study region.
properties.scienceReason: Impact craters provide stratigraphic context and can expose or redistribute subsurface materials.
properties.why: Officially named crater; the user's map reading [77.17, 18.13] is close to the USGS centre.
properties.survivalNote: Crater rims and ejecta can be rough or steep. The official centre is inside the current grid bounds, but this does not establish safe traversability.

properties.name: Angelica Crater
properties.description: IAU-adopted impact crater west of the current elevation grid.
properties.scienceReason: Impact structures provide geomorphic and stratigraphic context and may expose subsurface materials.
properties.why: Official centre is 76.95°E, 18.65°N; the user's supplied point [76.75, 18.64] is not the crater centre.
properties.survivalNote: Crater rim terrain may be steep; this crater is west of the current elevation grid and cannot be routed with that grid.

properties.name: Pliva Vallis
properties.description: Officially named valley on the eastern side of the Jezero region; the point is the USGS feature centre, not a point along a safe traverse.
properties.scienceReason: Its mapped valley morphology is relevant to reconstructing the regional drainage and lake history around Jezero.
properties.why: Important regional geomorphic feature, but the centre lies east of the current elevation grid.
properties.survivalNote: Valley walls and channel margins can be steep or rough; do not use the feature centre as a route waypoint.
